greeting: Is name_len bounded before any name byte is read?
Does UTF-8 decoding reject invalid lead bytes, truncated, bad-continuation, overlong, surrogate and above-U+10FFFF sequences while staying within name_len?
Does the printable check reject C0 controls, DEL and C1 controls?
Is every write to out bounded by capacity, and can the size arithmetic wrap?
Do all failure paths leave out[0] NUL when capacity > 0 and *written 0?
Does greeting_main bound the argument scan, handle a NULL name and report usage, status and write errors?

findings.property: out-of-bounds read of name when name_len exceeds the readable name buffer (for example SIZE_MAX)
findings.severity: high if real: read past a borrowed caller buffer
findings.rationale: Illustrative example entry for the hello-world example, not a record of a real external review. A caller can pass a name_len larger than the readable name bytes; the UTF-8 scan would then read past the buffer. source_identity is the sha256 of json.dumps({path: sha256}, sort_keys=True) over the example files under src/, include/, tests/project/, fuzz/project/, specs/project/ and review/ (paths relative to examples/hello-world, review/ledger.json excluded).
findings.reproducer: tests/project/test_greeting.c: expect(max, SIZE_MAX, 128U, GREETING_NAME_TOO_LONG, "") and expect(max, GREETING_NAME_MAX + 1U, ...)

history.reason: Not a defect: validate() rejects name_len > GREETING_NAME_MAX at src/greeting.c:100 before check_name() reads any byte; the SIZE_MAX and 65-byte boundary tests cover it and the fuzz target checks it for every input length.
